label: Tay–Sachs disease
description: Inherited HEXA dysfunction prevents normal breakdown of GM2, a fatty substance that builds up in nerve cells. Age of onset and severity vary.

label: Sandhoff disease
description: Inherited HEXB dysfunction reduces two related hexosaminidase enzymes. GM2 builds up in nerve cells, with additional substrates and sometimes more systemic involvement.

label: Niemann–Pick disease type C
description: Changes in NPC1 or NPC2 disrupt movement of cholesterol and other fats inside cells. Effects can involve the liver, spleen, movement, swallowing and cognition.

label: Gaucher disease
description: Reduced GBA1 enzyme activity causes fatty substances to accumulate, particularly in macrophages. Type 1 is primarily systemic; types 2 and 3 also affect the nervous system.

label: SPG11 hereditary spastic paraplegia
description: SPG11 variants disrupt spatacsin, a protein involved in cellular recycling. Long nerve fibers progressively malfunction, often causing leg stiffness, weakness and cognitive difficulties.
